commentary: John Wesley's Notes on the Bible
author: John Wesley

entries.title: Lamentations
entries.content: A widow - She that had a king, or rather a God, that was an husband to her, now was forsaken of God, and her king taken from her.

entries.title: Lamentations
entries.content: Because - Because of the servitude and oppression exercised among them: oppression by their rulers, and servitude more generally; keeping their servants beyond the year of jubilee, when they ought to be set at liberty. The straits - Those that pursued them overtook them in places where they could not escape.

entries.title: Lamentations
entries.content: She - Persons of all ages and ranks are in bitterness.

entries.title: Lamentations
entries.content: Pleasant things - Has laid violent hands on them. The things of the sanctuary were always pleasant things to those that feared God.

entries.title: Lamentations
entries.content: Bread - Even in a land that ordinarily flowed with milk and honey, they were at a loss for bread to eat. Given - And gave any thing for something to satisfy their hunger. Vile - Miserable or contemptible.

entries.title: Lamentations
entries.content: Is it nothing - The prophet speaks in the name of the Jewish church.

entries.title: Lamentations
entries.content: Fire - A judgment as consuming, and afflictive as fire.

entries.title: Lamentations
entries.content: Is bound - Put upon my neck on account of my transgressions. Wreathed - My punishments are twisted as cords; I have a complication of judgments upon me, sword, famine, pestilence, captivity.

entries.title: Lamentations
entries.content: An assembly - God had called an assembly of Chaldeans against the city, to crush the inhabitants of it. Trodden - God had trodden upon the Jews as men use to stamp grapes in a wine - press.

entries.title: Lamentations
entries.content: The comforter - God.

entries.title: Lamentations
entries.content: Jerusalem - Is become loathsome and filthy.

entries.title: Lamentations
entries.content: Deceived - They did not answer my expectation.

entries.title: Lamentations
entries.content: Death - By famine and pestilence.

entries.title: Lamentations
entries.content: They - The neighbouring nations. Like me - But thou hast foretold their destruction also, and hast by me proclaimed it: and thou shalt in that day bring them into as sad a condition as I am in now.

entries.title: Lamentations
entries.content: His footstool - His temple; but suffered the Chaldeans to destroy it. Cast down - That is, thrown them down from the highest glory and honour, to the meanest degree of servitude.

entries.title: Lamentations
entries.content: Polluted - Dealt with them as with a polluted thing; cast them off, brake them in pieces.

entries.title: Lamentations
entries.content: The horn - All their beauty and strength. Drawn back - God hath drawn back his assistance which he was wont to give the Jews against their enemies. Round about - God consumed them, not in this or that part, but round about, as a fire seizing an house at once on all sides.

entries.title: Lamentations
entries.content: His tabernacle - His temple. The places - The synagogues. The king - By the king and the priests are meant persons of greatest rank and eminency, though it is thought here is a special reference to Zedekiah the king of Judah, and Seraiah who was the high priest; the former of which was miserably handled, the latter slain.

entries.title: Lamentations
entries.content: They - The enemies with their triumphs and blasphemies, made as great a noise, as those that sang holy songs, or played on instruments, were wont to make to the glory of God.

entries.title: Lamentations
entries.content: The wall - The strength and security of the Jews. A line - Artificers used with lines not only to mark out places for building, but also for destruction, to direct them what to cut off; and such a line is here meant.

entries.title: Lamentations
entries.content: Among the Gentiles - In miserable captivity. The law - Is no more read, opened or observed. Her prophets - They had but very few prophets, from this time to the time of the gospel, and very few of those at this time alive had any revelation from God.

entries.title: Lamentations
entries.content: The virgins - The whole city is in a mournful posture.

entries.title: Lamentations
entries.content: Mine eyes - This whole verse is but expressive of the prophets great affliction for the miseries come upon the Jews. He wept himself almost blind. Bowels - His passion had disturbed his bodily humours, that his bowels were troubled. Liver - His gall lying under his liver. All these are expressions of great affliction and sorrow. Swoon - During the famine, occasioned by the long siege.

entries.title: Lamentations
entries.content: Bosom - When they died in their mother's arms.

entries.title: Lamentations
entries.content: Who - There was no people whose condition was in any degree parallel to the misery of the Jews: nor was there any cure for them, their breach was like a sea breach where the waters come in with such a torrent, that there is no making any defence against them.

entries.title: Lamentations
entries.content: The prophets - False prophets told you vain stories. Not discovered - Whereas they ought to have made you sensible of your sins, and this might have prevented your captivity. False burdens - False stories to encourage you in sin, and so cause your banishment.

entries.title: Lamentations
entries.content: O wall - That is, those that are upon it.

entries.title: Lamentations
entries.content: Whom - Not the Heathen, but to thy own people. Women - Wilt thou suffer women to satisfy their hunger with the fruit of their own bodies?

entries.title: Lamentations
entries.content: My terrors - As my people were wont to be called together from all parts in a solemn day, so now my terrible enemies, or terrible things are by thee called together.

entries.title: Lamentations
entries.content: I am the man - It seems, this is spoken in the name of the people, who were before set out under the notion of a woman.

entries.title: Lamentations
entries.content: Made old - All my beauty is gone, and all my strength.

entries.title: Lamentations
entries.content: Builded - He hath built forts and batteries against my walls and houses.

entries.title: Lamentations
entries.content: Enclosed - He has defeated all my methods and counsels for security, by insuperable difficulties like walls of hewn stone. Crooked - Nay, God not only defeated their counsels, but made them fatal and pernicious to them.

entries.title: Lamentations
entries.content: Wormwood - With severe and bitter dispensations.

entries.title: Lamentations
entries.content: Ashes - Mourners were wont to throw ashes on their heads.

entries.title: Lamentations
entries.content: Wormwood - Wormwood and gall, are often made use of to signify great affliction.

entries.title: Lamentations
entries.content: This - Which follows, concerning the nature of God, and his good providences.

entries.title: Lamentations
entries.content: Faithfulness - In fulfilling thy promises to thy people.

entries.title: Lamentations
entries.content: Bear - Quietly and patiently to bear what afflictions God will please to lay upon us. And if God tame us when young, by his word or by his rod, it is an unspeakable advantage.

entries.title: Lamentations
entries.content: Borne it - That he keep his soul in subjection to God, because God hath humbled him by his rod.

entries.title: Lamentations
entries.content: In the dust - Both this and the former verses let us know the duty of persons under afflictions.

entries.title: Lamentations
entries.content: Willingly - Not from his own mere motion without a cause given him from the persons afflicted. Hence judgment is called God's strange work.

entries.title: Lamentations
entries.content: To subvert - Here are three things mentioned, which God approveth not.

entries.title: Lamentations
entries.content: Who - Nothing comes to pass in the world, but by the disposal of divine providence. This seems to be spoken in the name of the people of God, arguing themselves into a quiet submission, to their afflictions, from the consideration of the hand of God in them.

entries.title: Lamentations
entries.content: Evil - Doth not evil or trouble come out of God's mouth from his direction, and providence, as well as good?

entries.title: Lamentations
entries.content: Wherefore - The Jews, check themselves in their complaints from the consideration, that nothing had befallen them, but what was the just reward of their sins.

entries.title: Lamentations
entries.content: Thou - Thou hast plagued us according to the just desert of our sins.

entries.title: Lamentations
entries.content: Mine eye - The prophet speaks this of himself.

entries.title: Lamentations
entries.content: Dungeon - Dungeon seems here to be taken for the lowest condition of misery.

entries.title: Lamentations
entries.content: Cut off - I am undone, there is no hope for me.

entries.title: Lamentations
entries.content: Heard - In former afflictions. Hide not - Shew me now the same favour.

entries.title: Lamentations
entries.content: O Lord - Thou hast been wont to take my part against my enemies.

entries.title: Lamentations
entries.content: Seen - Thou hast been a witness to all their fury.

entries.title: Lamentations
entries.content: I am - At feasts, and at their merry meetings, I am all the subject of their discourse.

entries.title: Lamentations
entries.content: Persecute - Many passages of this nature which we meet with are prophecies, some of them may be both prophecies and prayers.

entries.title: Lamentations
entries.content: The top - Are scattered in the head of every street.

entries.title: Lamentations
entries.content: Earthen pitchers - The nobles, the priests, and the good men, are looked upon no better than earthen vessels, the workmanship of an ordinary potter.

entries.title: Lamentations
entries.content: Cruel - The Jewish women are become cruel to their children, or forced to appear so, having through the famine no milk to give them, nor any thing to relieve them. Ostriches - Like ostriches that lay their eggs, and leave them in the sand.

entries.title: Lamentations
entries.content: Of Sodom - Their punishment was greater, because more lingering, and gradual, whereas Sodom was overthrown in a moment, and that by no human hands that abode upon her, causing her a continued torment.

entries.title: Lamentations
entries.content: Nazarites - Her Nazarites in this place signify her separated ones, who either in respect of birth, education, estate, or place of magistracy, were distinguished from the rest of the people.

entries.title: Lamentations
entries.content: Not known - So that those who before knew them, do not know them now.

entries.title: Lamentations
entries.content: Priests - The ecclesiastical men were a great cause of the first and last destruction of Jerusalem. And so they are of most other places that come to ruin, through their neglect of their duty, or encouraging others in their wicked courses.

entries.title: Lamentations
entries.content: They - The prophets and priests wandered up and down the streets polluting themselves with blood, either the blood of the children which they slew, or the just men, mentioned ver.13, the slaughter of whom they either encouraged, or at least did not discourage; so that one could not touch a prophet or priest, but he must be legally polluted, and there were so many of them, that men could not walk in the streets, but he must touch some of them.

entries.title: Lamentations
entries.content: Touch not - The Jews that made conscience of keeping the law against touching dead bodies, cried to the other Jews to leave the city as themselves did, the city being now so full of dead bodies that they could not stay in it without polluting themselves.

entries.title: Lamentations
entries.content: The anger - These words seem to be the language of their enemies triumphing over them. They - Their enemies had no regard to the most venerable persons among them.

entries.title: Lamentations
entries.content: A nation - The Egyptians.

entries.title: Lamentations
entries.content: They - The Chaldeans.

entries.title: Lamentations
entries.content: The anointed - Zedekiah, who though a bad man yet afforded some protection to the Jews. We said - We promised ourselves that though the land of Judah was encompassed with Pagan nations, yet through Zedekiah's valour and good conduct we should live comfortably.

entries.title: Lamentations
entries.content: Rejoice - The prophet speaks ironically, Rejoice; but thy joy shall be but for a little time. Drunken - Thou shalt be intoxicated with it, and make thyself naked as drunken men sometimes do.

entries.title: Lamentations
entries.content: Captivity - Not for thy past sins. Thy sins - By the punishment of them.

entries.title: Lamentations
entries.content: We - We are all of us without a king, (our common father) we are deprived of thy fatherly protection, and many young children among us are left without an earthly parent.
